HANDOFF for DrWrinch

Source: HANDOFF.md

Last touched: 2026-10-27. Read PLAN_decision_rule.md next. It records what changed in the paper between 2026-08-29 and 2026-10-19, the four choices Jake made on 2026-10-27, the tests written before the code, and the edits the paper repository needs once this version is on GitHub.

What DrWrinch is

The R package implementing Lopez, Bowers, and Gajardo Cooper (2026), “Fully specified Bayes factors for process tracing.” The paper is in ~/repos/fully_specified_bf and is the source of truth for notation and methods. Named after Dorothy Maud Wrinch (1894–1976), whose joint papers with Harold Jeffreys developed the framework that became Jeffreys’s theory of Bayes factors. The companion package DrBristol (~/repos/DrBristol) implements p-value methods for the same problems; the two stay separate.

State of the package, 2026-10-27

Version 0.0.2.1, uncommitted. devtools::test() passes 134 tests (1101 expectations) with no warnings, and devtools::check() reports 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes. The local app was run in a browser: both tabs render, and the only console error is the missing favicon.

The paper’s rule sets the rival aside, at least provisionally, when the uniform-weights Bayes factor is 20 or more and the worst-case Bayes factor is above 1. The exported functions follow it:

  • bf_uniform_weights(y_W, y_R, omega), in R/bf_uniform_weights.R.
  • bf_worst_case(y_W, y_R, omega, a1, b1), in R/bf_worst_case.R. Under bias it divides by the largest probability any rival share gives the counts, which moves below a share of one half once omega > y_W / y_R (Jake’s decision of 2026-10-27; the paper’s five affected table cells are to be recomputed to match). When y_W < y_R the rival stays at one half, as in the paper’s closed form.
  • bf_rescaled(), in R/bf_rescaled.R.
  • bf_uniform_weights_finite() and bf_worst_case_finite(), in R/bf_finite.R, for an archive of known size.
  • sens_bias() and sens_coding(), in R/sens_bias.R and R/sens_coding.R. Each returns the tipping point for each condition of the rule and the smaller of the two.
  • run_app(), in R/run_app.R.

Removed in this version, without deprecation because no one else uses the package: bf_binomial(), bf_urn(), sens_urn(), sens_binomial(), bf_separated(), separation_g(), bf_separated_bias(), and the deprecation helper. BiasedUrn, ggplot2, and dplyr left DESCRIPTION.

The Shiny app (inst/shiny/) takes two thresholds, opens the Result tab with what the rule decides, and on the Sensitivity tab reports the coding and bias tipping points under the rule beside one plot of both Bayes factors against the bias. .dw_needed in inst/shiny/global.R is 0.0.2.1.

The paper repository

The paper still sources its own tests/*.R. Two cross-checks in its tests/bf_weighted.R call DrWrinch::bf_binomial() and DrWrinch::bf_urn(), so the paper, the supplement, and the replications will stop with an error as soon as the paper’s renv library installs this version. PLAN_decision_rule.md lists those fixes, the supplement’s reproduction section rewrite, the renv.lock update, and the five worst-case cells. The current arXiv preprint’s reproduction section calls removed functions, so the next arXiv replacement is what brings the preprint and the package back into agreement.

Deployment failures and their fixes

  • Stale GITHUB_PAT in ~/.Renviron (commented out 2026-05-19, with a note pointing to https://github.com/settings/tokens for a fresh one). If remotes::install_github ever falls back to anonymous unexpectedly, check that this token still works.
  • shinyapps.io’s “401 fetching GitHub” failure mode is almost always a stale OAuth cache, not a missing PAT. The toggle-on / toggle-off cycle in Posit Authentication is the fix.
  • shinyapps.io’s “stale DrWrinch / function-not-found” failure mode (hit and fixed 2026-06-22). shinyapps installs DrWrinch into the read-only system library (/usr/lib/R) at image-build time from its manifest, and that copy can lag GitHub HEAD. A runtime install_github cannot overwrite it (mv ... Permission denied, “cannot remove earlier installation, is it in use?”), so the app silently keeps the old version and errors on any newer function (this session: 'sens_coding' is not an exported object). The symptom is a tab-level “An error has occurred” with the plots still rendering, and the real cause is only visible via rsconnect::showLogs(). Fix in inst/shiny/global.R: install the required version into a writable, session-local library (tempdir()) placed FIRST on .libPaths(), shadowing the stale system copy. Check the installed version with packageVersion() — NOT requireNamespace(), which loads the old namespace and then blocks library() from picking up the reinstall. The GitHub download and build succeed at runtime; only the install location has to be writable. Each cold start spends about 30 seconds on this install. When the required version changes, bump .dw_needed in global.R.
  • rsconnect refuses to bundle locally-installed packages that lack RemoteType metadata. Trying to dodge GitHub via a local tarball doesn’t work cleanly; the right workarounds are
    1. fix the OAuth cache (what worked this session), (b) R-universe.
  • The Shiny app pulls DrWrinch from GitHub on shinyapps.io cold start via the install_github stanza in inst/shiny/global.R, about 30 seconds per cold start. Local development skips it, because devtools::load_all() has already loaded the current version.

Still open

  • inst/CITATION points to the arXiv preprint (arXiv:2606.16683). Add the journal DOI when the paper is published.
  • The app has no shinytest2 snapshot tests. The helpers and the reactive graph are tested through testthat and shiny::testServer().
  • GitHub authentication is switched off in Posit’s settings. Publishing to Posit Cloud would need it switched on again.
